title: Bienvenut to "Vostre Altesse" (the duc de Nevers?), Paris, 28 February 1590 (BnF fr. 3623 no. 23; DECODE R9453)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's nevers.htm and GL.htm, DECODE list for fr. 3623/3625; no prior reading; DECODE gives folios.
Gallica thumbnails of both volumes; contact sheets; full-resolution pages of ff. 35-41, 88, 111 (fr. 3623) and ff. 10, 16 (fr. 3625).
No. 23: key slip on f. 36r transcribed; every code number in the letter resolves.
The 26 code numbers of ff. 35r-v listed in text order from the full-resolution images (codes.txt); all nine values occur on the key slip f. 36r (key.txt).

Entry split from champagne1590 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 23's name code (35 = Mayenne, 37 = M. de Nemours, 53 = Saint-Sorlin) conflicts with the two-digit alphabet of nos. 24/25/60 (35 = a, 37 = c, 53 = i), so it is a different key.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): codes.txt + key.txt as transcription; decryption sample copied from NOTES.md to texts/n23_decryption.md; the full clear text of ff. 35r-v is not yet transcribed

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/n23_decryption.md is a sample of fragments joined by "..."; it reads, but most of the letter is not transcribed. Kept read for the sample with an excerpt note; class read -> read in part; fraction_read 1.0 -> about 0.15 (estimated).

Consistency pass (cl): 'read in part' not justified because ff. 35r-v beyond the sample are genuinely untranscribed (not-attempted kept) and the retry step is not done; NOTES already Status: in progress; outcome.gaps already mirrors the list.

Full diplomatic transcription of ff. 35r-v from the full-resolution Gallica images (canvases 79-80), read line by line in 2x crops: 33 + 35 lines, abbreviations expanded in [ ], struck words kept as ~~ ~~, 17 doubtful words marked (texts/n23_transcription.md; 1,259 tokens measured). The 26 code numbers fall where codes.txt lists them (15 recto, 11 verso).

Key slip f. 36r applied to the full text (texts/n23_decryption.md): all 26 codes resolve and read in their sentences. The dual entries resolved by context: 15 = Provence & Dauphine at 35v.09 ('qu'elle y remedie en 15'); 17 = Picardie at 35r.30 ('veuille empieter 17') and 35v.19 ('menees qu'ilz font en 17'); at 35r.28 (Ambassadeurs de 15) and 35v.33 (harquebuziers des meilleurs de 17) both values are kept.

Measured on the full reading: read_share 0.985 (962 words, 1 hole, 13 doubtful; research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.share); docs/_check_reading.py clean sentences 0.80 (73/91). Above the 95% read bar; class read in part -> read.

Recipient: the full text points to Charles-Emmanuel I of Savoy rather than Nevers (Bienvenut signs as 'subject' of Vostre Altesse; Gex and the siege of Bonne 'qui nous travaille', both Savoyard places under Genevan/Bernese attack 1589-90; 'remedy in Provence & Dauphine'; the Altesse's 'ministres' in Paris kept out by Mendoza and Moreo). Web search for Bienvenut as a Savoyard agent in Paris 1590 found nothing; hypothesis only.

Second pass: native-resolution crops of the 13 doubtful words. Settled 8 (emotions, Roccas, Vier, style, cogneu, occurrances, a, que); corrected 2 (35r.24 affectionnes -> affaires; 35r.26 unread word -> 'de bon lieu', 'ne part' struck); 4 words and the 35v.20 heading stay doubtful.
Re-measured the reading: read_share 0.985 -> 0.996 (963 words, 0 unread, 4 doubtful); _check_reading.py 0.80 -> 0.84 clean sentences (76/90).

Bienvenu found as secretary of Charles-Emmanuel I of Savoy, engaged with the League, in Lucinge, Lettres sur les debuts de la Ligue (1585), ed. Dufour, Droz 1964; recipient Savoy now probable. Roccas, Vier and M. de Riddes not found (Lesdiguieres/Dauphine 1590, Geneva-Savoy war 1589-90 searches).

Independent check (14 Nov 2026, Brice Dudout with Claude): a separate script resolves the 26 code numbers of texts/n23_transcription.md on key.txt and they match the 26 bracketed names of texts/n23_decryption.md one for one; the 26 numbers read again on Gallica canvases 79-80 at full size, all as transcribed; 35r.11 and 35r.29 seen again, both stay doubtful; read share recounted 0.996 as recorded.

Integration check of PR #559 (14 Nov 2026): own script resolves the 26 codes of texts/n23_transcription.md on key.txt, same order as codes.txt, one for one with the 26 names of texts/n23_decryption.md; f. 35r codes (15) seen on Gallica canvas 79 as transcribed; v10_relabel.share 963 words, 0 holes, 4 doubtful, 0.996, as recorded.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Measured 27 Oct 2026 on the full reading texts/n23_decryption.md after the second pass: read_share = 1 - (holes + doubtful)/(words + holes) = 0.996 (963 words, 0 unread, 4 doubtful; research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.share). All 26 code numbers resolve from the key slip; at 2 of them (35r.28 '15', 35v.33 '17') the slip's dual value is not settled by context and both values are given.
outcome.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from champagne1590. The copy is in clear except for nine name codes; it reports the League court in Paris (Madame de Nemours, Saint-Sorlin, the Pope and Spain, Mayenne). 22 Oct 2026 reading audit: only a sample was transcribed (read in part). 26 Oct 2026: ff. 35r-v transcribed in full and read, read_share 0.985; 27 Oct second pass 0.996. The writer is probably Bienvenu, secretary of Charles-Emmanuel I of Savoy (Lucinge's letters, 1585), and the recipient the Duke of Savoy (probable, see NOTES).

texts.label: Paris, 28 Feb 1590, BnF fr. 3623 no. 23, ff. 35r-v (key f. 36r)
texts.summary: Bienvenut reports from Paris to 'Vostre Altesse' (probably Charles-Emmanuel I of Savoy, whose secretary Bienvenu was) that Madame de Nemours wants her son Nemours in Spanish service or back in his government; that news has come of Grenoble, Gex and the siege of Bonne; that the Pope, Spain and Mayenne have agreed Spain's aid will pass through the Pope, who is to send 8 or 10,000 men; that Mendoza and Moreo keep the Altesse's ministers out of affairs; and, in cipher, that he means to leave Paris in March with Nemours's troops, and can raise 1,000-1,200 arquebusiers.
texts.note: Full text of ff. 35r-v, transcribed 26 Oct 2026, doubtful words re-read at native resolution 27 Oct 2026 (texts/n23_transcription.md, diplomatic, folio and line); 4 doubtful words and the 35v.20 heading marked.

reading_review.note: Second pass at native resolution: 8 doubtful words settled, 2 corrected (affaires, de bon lieu); _check_reading.py 0.84 clean (76/90); the failing sentences are long run-on periods and the 4 doubtful words.

prior.where: the key slip bound after the copy, f. 36r; the copy itself is in clear except the code numbers
